pre_mortem: A strong solver reads the 112-line ordinance, writes a reference billing model in integers, and fuzzes the package against it. Every departure (half-up rounding, true-up from the previous read, per-unit per-day service charge, block scaling, household sewer allowance, sewer on cubic feet, day-weighted proration) is fully stated, so its reference converges on all seven. It goes wrong only where its own reference encodes a reach decision: when writing the width loop it scales every span (the service charge right above is scaled for every span), and when writing the sewer cap it caps every account (every account carries winter spans). Its fuzzing then agrees with its own over-reach. It is right if it stops at 2.3 and 2.4.
decisive_reason: two independent loop-uniform traps whose bounds sit in separate section-2 definitions, each against a governed rule that scales or multiplies for every span/account; both are one hop for a solver that reads each rule's subject term, which is why confidence is low.
